name: Supply — scope under the CGST Act
definition: For the purposes of the CGST Act the expression 'supply' includes all forms of supply of goods or services or both — sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal — made or agreed to be made for a consideration by a person in the course or furtherance of business; the import of services for a consideration whether or not in the course or furtherance of business; and the activities specified in Schedule I made or agreed to be made without a consideration. Activities specified in Schedule III are treated neither as a supply of goods nor as a supply of services.
why_it_exists: Nothing else in GST can start without it. Time of supply (s.12, s.13) and value of supply (s.15) both presuppose that a supply exists, and s.9(1) levies the tax on supplies at the value determined under s.15. If the transaction is not a supply, no GST entry is posted at all — so this is the first gate, not a detail.

common_mistakes: concluding 'no consideration, therefore no supply' — Schedule I overrides that (s.7(1)(c))
treating an import of services as outside GST because it was not for business — s.7(1)(b) says otherwise
deciding goods-versus-services from the invoice wording instead of Schedule II — the branch decides whether s.12 or s.13 applies, and therefore the tax point
assuming a supply exists because an accounting entry exists — an accrual is not a supply

examples: goods sold for a price by a trader in the course of business — a supply under s.7(1)(a)
services imported for a consideration by a person not in business — still a supply under s.7(1)(b)
counterexamples: an activity specified in Schedule III — treated neither as a supply of goods nor a supply of services under s.7(2)(a), so no GST entry arises
